cases.mechanism: _extract_answer lowercases the whole text (text_lower = text.lower().strip()) before running re.search(r'\\boxed\{([^}]+)\}', text_lower). A non-LaTeX '\BOXED{yes}' inside <think> therefore becomes the first '\boxed{yes}' match, so accuracy_reward and partial_match_reward score 1. format_reward finds the real '\boxed{no}' (its regex uses re.IGNORECASE) together with <think>, so it scores 1. The think block is over 200 characters and the response hits 4 evidence patterns. Total 1.0.
cases.why_incorrect: The only real \boxed{} in the response is \boxed{no}, and the gold answer is yes. A case-sensitive verifier sees 'no' and marks it wrong. A case-insensitive verifier sees two boxes with different contents, which is also incorrect.
